title: Case: Recipient who collected a garden bench from the depot himself writes about the costs
context: Cosmo Gallimore ordered a cast-iron garden bench from Gorsewick Goods (TG-7714 / DL-3547) with paid home delivery. He collected it from the Ashgrove Arc depot himself after a failed attempt.
initial_request: I now hold two letters and I invite you to read them side by side. (1) Your carrier's investigators, 13 May: 'The attempt was made at the wrong location... Ashgrove Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error.' (2) Your carrier's customer relations, 17 May: no compensation, final response. So fault is admitted in terms and the remedy for it is nil. Remarkable. I paid 14.50 for delivery to my home. That service was not performed; I performed it, over 38 miles, in my own car. I require written confirmation from you by 17:00 tomorrow that the 14.50 and my mileage will be refunded. A further apology will not be treated as a response. I have had three.

events.body: TG-7714 dispatched with Ashgrove Arc as DL-3547. Service: home delivery, charged to the customer at our checkout at 14.50. For reference, delivery charges on our orders are ours; any refund of one is decided by Refunds team, Gorsewick Goods, on evidence of a service failure.
DL-3547 attempted 13:20 today. Driver note: no access, carded. Held at Destination depot. Next re-delivery slot on that route is 16 May.

For the record. I was at home throughout 10 May. No card was left. My door camera shows no vehicle between 12:00 and 15:00. As the next slot offered was six days away I drove to your depot this morning and collected DL-3547 myself: a round trip of 38 miles. I should like the attempt examined.

Please review the 10 May 12:20 stop for DL-3547. The recipient, Cosmo Gallimore, says he was home, no card was left and his camera shows no vehicle. He has since collected the parcel from the depot himself. Please confirm what the route record shows.

DL-3547 reviewed. Stop GPS for 10 May 12:20 places the driver at Harrow Fold Lane. The delivery address is Harrow Fold Close. The attempt was made at the wrong location and no card was left at the correct address. Ashgrove Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error. This finding has been sent to the recipient in writing today.

Copied to the Rivet Delivery Desk. Dear Mr Gallimore, we are sorry for the failed delivery of DL-3547. Under our conditions of carriage Ashgrove Arc does not pay recipients' travel costs or other consequential losses. The delivery charge was set and collected by the sender, not by us, and we hold none of it. This is Ashgrove Arc's final response on compensation.

I now hold two letters and I invite you to read them side by side. (1) Your carrier's investigators, 13 May: 'The attempt was made at the wrong location... Ashgrove Arc accepts that the failed delivery was our error.' (2) Your carrier's customer relations, 17 May: no compensation, final response. So fault is admitted in terms and the remedy for it is nil. Remarkable. I paid 14.50 for delivery to my home. That service was not performed; I performed it, over 38 miles, in my own car. I require written confirmation from you by 17:00 tomorrow that the 14.50 and my mileage will be refunded. A further apology will not be treated as a response. I have had three.

Refund decision requested on the delivery charge for TG-7714 / DL-3547 (Cosmo Gallimore, cast-iron garden bench, home delivery charged at 14.50). Ashgrove Arc attempted delivery on 10 May. Delivery investigations confirmed in writing on 13 May that the driver was at Harrow Fold Lane, not Harrow Fold Close, that no card was left at the correct address, and that Ashgrove Arc accepts the failed delivery was its error. The next re-delivery slot was six days out, so Mr Gallimore collected the parcel from the depot himself on 11 May, a 38-mile round trip. Ashgrove Arc customer relations told him on 17 May that it pays no travel costs and holds none of the delivery charge, and called that its final response. He is asking for the 14.50 delivery charge and his mileage. Your dispatch note says delivery-charge refunds are yours to decide on evidence of a service failure: please decide on the charge and tell me your position on the mileage. He has had the admission and three apologies and no remedy from anyone, and has asked for an answer by 17:00 on 19 May. I have promised him nothing.
FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Refunds team, Gorsewick Goods restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Promises or implies that the 14.50 delivery charge, the mileage or any other compensation will be paid, or commits to his 17:00 deadline
Sends Cosmo Gallimore another apology that names no owner and no next step
Tells him the matter is closed because the carrier has given its final response
Questions or waters down the admitted fault, for example by suggesting the driver may have attended or that he should have waited for the 16 May re-delivery

rationale: Rule-made from gen-3201: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 8) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed.
